title: Git LFS SSH URL handling can inject commands on the remote host
summary: Git LFS fails to quote the path in SSH object-transfer and authentication commands. A crafted remote URL can inject commands if the remote SSH service passes them to a shell without sanitization.

severity.rationale: Remote command execution depends on remote service command handling. SSH-based source workflows commonly meet the transport prerequisite.

exposure: The remote SSH endpoint must execute unsanitized commands. This flaw concerns commands sent to the remote host, not unconditional local execution.

params.instructions: Check Git LFS version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 3.8.1 or later. Disabling SSH transfers alone does not prevent SSH authentication requests; remote services must also sanitize incoming commands.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
